subject.title: [Feature] Prime-number default scheduling for HEARTBEAT / cron “every” + deterministic per-agent phase jitter (anti top-of-hour spikes)

question: Should OpenClaw add public phase, jitter, or prime-cadence controls for cron `every` schedules, or keep `every` as a fixed anchored interval and limit anti-herd behavior to heartbeat plus cron expressions?
rationale: The remaining work changes public scheduling semantics and persisted config shape, and repository policy treats config/default additions and setup surfaces as compatibility-sensitive product decisions.

options.title: Design a narrow cron every phase contract
options.body: Add one explicit `every` phase/stagger contract with schema, CLI, docs, persistence, and upgrade tests before implementation.

options.title: Keep every fixed
options.body: Preserve `every` as a fixed anchored interval and rely on heartbeat phase plus cron-expression stagger for anti-herd behavior.

options.title: Accept a broader prime mode
options.body: Add prime cadence transforms plus deterministic phase controls for heartbeat and cron, with migration and observability requirements.

recommendation.title: Design a narrow cron every phase contract
recommendation.body: Add one explicit `every` phase/stagger contract with schema, CLI, docs, persistence, and upgrade tests before implementation.

likelyOwner.reason: The current cron stagger surface and docs were introduced in their commit, so they are the strongest routing candidate for the cron scheduling product boundary.
